draft.shortGloss: to go up; to climb; to rise
notes: The stem vowel 'u' changes to open 'o' (/ɔ/) in the singular and third-person plural of the present tense: 'eu subo', but 'você sobe', 'eles sobem'.
Use 'subir em' for getting onto or climbing something ('subir na árvore', 'subir no ônibus'), and 'subir' directly for stairs or streets ('subir a escada').

senses.definition: To move from a lower place to a higher one, or to get onto something.

examples.text: Eu preciso subir as escadas para chegar ao escritório.
examples.translation: I need to go up the stairs to get to the office.
examples.emotion: matter-of-fact and focused on the task at hand

examples.text: O menino gosta de subir na árvore do quintal.
examples.translation: The boy likes to climb the tree in the backyard.
examples.emotion: playful and adventurous, recalling a childhood activity

senses.definition: To become higher in level, amount, or price.

examples.text: O preço da gasolina vai subir amanhã.
examples.translation: The price of gasoline will go up tomorrow.
examples.emotion: mildly concerned or resigned to bad news

draftBefore.shortGloss: to go up; to climb; to increase
notes: Subir is a very flexible verb. While it primarily means to move towards a higher place, it is also used for prices rising or increasing volume.

senses.definition: To move from a lower place to a higher one.

examples.text: Eu preciso subir as escadas para chegar ao escritório.
examples.translation: I need to go up the stairs to get to the office.
examples.emotion: matter-of-fact and focused on the task at hand

senses.definition: To move upward using both hands and feet to grip or hold on.

examples.text: O menino gosta de subir na árvore do quintal.
examples.translation: The boy likes to climb the tree in the backyard.
examples.emotion: playful and adventurous, recalling a childhood activity

senses.definition: To increase in level, price, or intensity.

examples.text: O preço da gasolina vai subir amanhã.
examples.translation: The price of gasoline will rise tomorrow.
examples.emotion: mildly concerned or resigned to bad news

faults.why: Word-final 'r' in standard Brazilian Portuguese is not a tap /ɾ/, but /ʁ/ (often dropped).
